args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. Mitigation: checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy with an error rate of ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and find out why it was promoted even though staging was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened incident INC-0001. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** The failing release was v2.3.1, which had an error rate of about 18%. I moved us-east, us-west and eu-west back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. No change-manager approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Check afterwards:** checkout-api now reports healthy in all three regions, with the error rate down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open as a SEV2 for checkout-api, and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure and the rollback.
- **Follow-up:** The incident also asks for two things: the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and why v2.3.1 reached production even though its test build was already failing in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (previously healthy, so no approval needed).
